chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a woman who makes her female slave girl permissible (for intercourse) for her husband. He said: 'I dislike this.' I said: 'If she becomes pregnant?' He said: 'You say: If she becomes pregnant by you, then it is for you.' He said: 'There is no problem with this.' I said: 'So a man does this with his brother?' He said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.تُحِلُّ فَرْجَ: makes permissible the private part (for intercourse)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the juristic ruling on a master permitting another man to have intercourse with his female slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *tamlik al-farj* (granting sexual access) regarding female slaves (*jawari*), addressing the specific legal mechanism for attributing paternity in cases of shared use. His initial expression of *karahah* (dis/preference) rather than prohibition highlights the nuanced Shia view on the practicality and social implications of this practice, which was common in pre-Islamic and early Islamic societies. The ruling's extension to a man allowing another man to use his slave underscores the property rights aspect of the female slave in Shia jurisprudence, distinct from the marital bond.
